## NEW FINDINGS

The rejection rests on findings 1 to 3; findings 4 to 7 are smaller but each is a real point of the binding rulings or of the repository's own rules. Anchors spot-checked and found real: `review.graph.build_cached_graph` (custodian/src/eii_custodian/publicdata/review/graph.py), S2-T01, S2-T14, S2-T19, S2-T21, S2-T25 (whose shared fetch helpers S2-T27's scope also names), S2-T27, S2-T28 and S2-T29 as headings; decisions 0026 and 0034 files; OI-136 to OI-139 in document 04; the "eleven of the twelve" sentence is consistent in the record's Consequences, the TASKS.md slice S2 gate, and document 14's paragraph, task lines and gate line. No sentence in the new material claims a fetch, a count or a gate result; the advisor's readings carry their reader and date, and counts stay leads.

**Finding 1 — S2-T28's base criteria contradict the L-707 carry.** File: TASKS.md; place: S2-T28, the Goal and acceptance boxes 1 and 4. Defect: the Goal still reads "Lift each, with the facts it needs, so that `./eii build-public` fetches it through the normal seam with a receipt and a hash"; box 1 still reads "each of the twelve rows has its skip reason removed and carries publisher, licence id and basis, URL, fetch host, extension…"; box 4 still reads "the accident dataset fetches in bounded pages with one receipt…". All three demand that the accident row be lifted, skip-free and fetched, which the fix's own amendment line forbids ("the accident row is not activated here… the row keeps a skip reason `partition_byte_bound_unconfirmed`… built and tested offline", L-707 K1) and the gate sentence contradicts ("Eleven of the twelve… the accident table's year-partition plan and refusals pass offline"). A reviewer ticking box 1 must fail the correct build, or pass a wrong one. Exact fix: amend the Goal and boxes 1 and 4 to except the accident row — for example, Goal: "…fetches it through the normal seam with a receipt and a hash; the accident row is the exception: its year-partition plan, receipt and refusals are built and tested offline and its activation is S2-T29's through S2-T25's shared bounded reader (L-707 item K1)"; box 1: "each of the twelve rows has its resolved skip reason removed — the accident row then carries `partition_byte_bound_unconfirmed` until S2-T29 — and carries publisher…"; box 4: "the accident dataset's bounded-page fetch is planned offline with one receipt that names every page and its hash and a total that must equal the published count, or the fetch is refused (planted short page, planted duplicate page); it is not activated in this task".

**Finding 2 — L-708 item 2's press-figure clause is carried nowhere.** File: TASKS.md (and docs/04_PUBLIC_DATA_PACK.md); place: S2-T29's fix amendment, private-school item, and the school rows of document 04. Defect: L-708 rules "the press-reported seat figure is no feed"; the change carries the user-agent, browser-driven capture, access-failure recording and one-line-tell clauses, but no passage excludes a press-reported seat or capacity figure as a feed — the amendment's "no figure stands in for the directory" sits inside the access-failure branch, and the school rows guard only what the directory itself supplies. Exact fix: add to the private-school item of the S2-T29 amendment line (and, in one clause, to the school rows of document 04 section 2.4 and section 12): "the press-reported seat figure is no feed: no press-reported capacity or seat figure is registered, fetched or shown".

**Finding 3 — L-709's tools clause is carried nowhere.** File: TASKS.md; place: S2-T29's fix amendment, awards item. Defect: L-709 rules "tools get only the advisor's aggregate profile, never a row"; the amendment carries "no value of the workbook is committed and tests use invented rows", which governs commits and tests but not what a build tool may read of the real workbook. Exact fix: add to the awards item: "builder tools receive only the advisor's aggregate profile of the workbook, never a row of it".

**Finding 4 — L-709's supplier-certification-gap mapping is carried nowhere.** File: docs/decisions/0046 (and docs/04_PUBLIC_DATA_PACK.md); place: item 8 and the `awards_owner_scrape` row. Defect: L-709 states the awards source "serves backlog item 9 and the supplier-certification gap"; no passage maps the awards source to the supplier-certification gap (N6, OI-138), which is a repository anchor. The "backlog item 9" half has no repository anchor (the repository's backlog item 9 is the product-space context line, a different thing), so leaving that half out or rewording it without a false anchor is right; the supplier-certification half is carryable and uncarried. Exact fix: add one clause to record item 8 or the `awards_owner_scrape` row: "the awards source serves the supplier-certification gap (N6, OI-138) as evidence, without closing it".

**Finding 5 — the Decision list numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 6, 7 in that order.** File: docs/decisions/0046; place: Decision section, item 8 physically sits between items 5 and 6. Defect: rule 33 anchors a decision record by its numbered items, and a Markdown renderer renumbers a loose ordered list sequentially, so the rendered awards item becomes "item 6", colliding with the written item 6 that document 14 cites as "decision 0046 items 5 and 6"; raw-text and rendered readers get different referents. Exact fix: move item 8 to the end of the Decision list, after item 7; its number stays 8 and the sequence becomes 1 to 8.

**Finding 6 — L-707 K3's birth-year point is carried only conditionally.** File: docs/decisions/0046; place: Proposed open items (with TASKS.md S2-T28's amendment line). Defect: K3 reads "the birth-year use is a proposed open item", stated flat; the change carries only L-701 G3's conditional ("joins `caveat_keys` only where a key for that use exists, otherwise it is a proposed open item"), so if a caveat key for that use exists at build time, the still-binding "never used by a card until a later ruling" question is tracked nowhere. Exact fix: add a proposed open item, for example "OI-[LEAD-8] — Accident perpetrator birth-year use: whether any card may use `birth_year_of_accident_perpetr`, and under which caveat key, is a proposed open item; no card uses the column until it is answered."

**Finding 7 — rule 37: the school access-failure guard has no planted violation.** File: TASKS.md; place: S2-T29's fix amendment, private-school item. Defect: the item requires the access failure to be recorded with its date, but names no planted case; every other guard of the fix names one. Exact fix: append "(a planted connection reset asserts the failure is recorded with its date)" to that item.

**Why rejected:** findings D1 to D7 are all genuinely fixed, and the fix is a competent fold-in of the three rulings. **F1 — S7-T24 must be Deep: it computes and releases numbers.**

(S2-T30's Standard is correct and must not change: it parses, archives and reports source state and computes no released figure.)
- Exact fix: in TASKS.md replace the S7-T24 Delivery line with: `- Delivery: Deep; reason: the task computes and releases new numbers — service-catchment shortlists, whole-cell population sums and reach sets — on audience surfaces, which the delivery-class rule makes Deep; no ingress or privacy control changes. Builder persona: senior applied economist and calculation engineer; strict reviewer persona: principal economic-methods and provenance reviewer from another maker; status queued.` In docs/14_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md's slice S7 task list, change the S7-T24 row's `Standard; full criteria and personas: TASKS.md, S7-T24.` to `Deep; full criteria and personas: TASKS.md, S7-T24.`

**F2 — S7-T01's amended Depends omit S2-T19, the fetcher of two sources its new amendments name.**
- File: TASKS.md. Place: S7-T01, Depends line (amended by this record).
- Defect: Amendment A4 names dated `hotel_ext` room-supply and rate context and A5 names `survey_ext` activity accounts. Both are fetched only by S2-T19 (docs/04's hotel_ext row, "to fetch in S2-T19", and PUB-108; decision 0046 item 4 confirms neither is one of S2-T28's twelve rows). The record added S2-T11, S2-T28 and S4-T09 to S7-T01's Depends for the other named inputs of the same amendments, but not S2-T19, while S7-T08 and S7-T07 carry explicit S2-T19 wiring for the same sources. The listed Depends therefore do not carry the amendments' own inputs; the slice-gate path through S6-T05 is not source wiring.
- Exact fix: change `- Depends: S6-T05, S2-T12, S2-T11, S2-T28, S4-T09.` to `- Depends: S6-T05, S2-T12, S2-T11, S2-T19, S2-T28, S4-T09.`

Readings taken, stated for the record: "Deep where they compute or release numbers" binds the Delivery class of the tasks this record classifies (the two new tasks; amended tasks keep their untouched legacy class), and "Depends real" requires the amended dependency list to carry the inputs the record's own amendments name.

### S1-T20 — The hosted mutation pilot: task log (pull request https://github.com/albarami/economic-investment-intelligence/pull/75 )

- What it is and why it exists: a runner-tooling task added to slice S1 by a re-plan of 2026-11-16, as S1-T19 was. It adds one manually dispatched workflow, `.github/workflows/mutation-pilot.yml`, that runs the mutation campaign of one named module in four deterministic hosted shards, and the script `scripts/mutation_pilot.py`, which validates the dispatch input, regenerates the mutant universe, partitions it by exact mutant name, transports each shard's evidence, merges the four parts against the manifest and judges survivors against `scripts/mutation_explained.toml`, and compares a hosted report with an unpartitioned local report of the same commit. The workflow is dispatch only, holds a read-only token, uses only action pins the three required workflows already use, reads no secret and is not a required check. The local command `scripts/mutation.py` keeps its command and output; it gains only the regenerated-universe identity check that the merge needs.

Lens A: independent test-infrastructure and mutation-testing correctness reviewer, Moonshot Kimi K3.1 Pro through Droid. Lens B: independent continuous-integration security reviewer (GitHub Actions supply chain, token permissions, injection through workflow inputs), Google Gemini 3.1 Pro through Droid. Lead: Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5 (plan ruling, verification, commits of the builder's changes, records).
- Skills (rules 34 and 43). Builder: task-standards, project-orientation, github-flow, sharp-edges, muhasabah-gate; the brief carried the rules of test-driven development, security review and verification before completion where the tool lacked them. Lens A: strict-reviewer, mutation-testing, spec-to-code-compliance, sharp-edges, muhasabah-gate, with the plain rule of code-review. 3. The target split puts `x_p_part = 1` on a stayer part, because the leaver parts have `K = 0`. Its `w_p_q_part = 0.01 <= Q_stay = 0` then fails.

**Without the parts, the model is FEASIBLE and admits the planted cohort.** Here "without the parts" means item 11 as it stood at 710ac47: cohort counts with wage sums, and "the later month's variables equal the earlier month's after those cohorts".

- The count holds: `1 = 1 + 0`.
- The month-`m` wage holds: `0.01 = 0 + 0.01`.
- Month `m+1` holds: `W = 0.01 - 0.01 + (stayer wage sum at m+1 - 0) + 0`, met with a stayer wage sum at `m+1` equal to the tuple's `W` at `m+1`.
- Nothing ties a zero count to a zero wage sum.

## FINDINGS

### Finding 1: `docs/06_PRIVACY_AND_DISCLOSURE_CONTROL.md`, PRV-113 item 11 (also PRV-56, ASSUMPTION 33, DAT-137)

**Defect.**

- The parts exist "for each pair of adjacent months `m` and `m+1`".
- Every published cohort must be "the sum of the parts whose origin, destination and employer-group-change status match it".
- After a unit and tier are carried forward, "the next comparison runs from the month the release shows". PRV-56 enumerates its cohorts "always against the month whose treated atoms the release shows for that unit and tier", and DAT-137 publishes them as the row's components.
- That comparison spans more than one month. No part covers it, and the adjacent parts do not sum to its cohorts.
- The true assignment is therefore infeasible. Any assignment that meets the cohort equalities moves the count of the carried-forward month away from the truth.
- This contradicts PRV-121: "A reduction that changes the feasible set of any target expression is a defect". The model must contain the truth.

**Failing input** (invented, set A, `residence`):

1. Unit U is a cell unit of `rp_all_count`. It has 100 earners in month `m`, each in a different employer group of the aggregate class.
2. Between `m` and `m+1`, 5 earners join from "outside the frame" and 6 leave to it. Both cohorts are below `min_earners_count` (10), so PRV-56 carries U forward.
3. The `(m, m+1)` row is `carried_forward`, and month `m+1` repeats month `m`'s treated atoms. The true month-`m+1` count is 99.
4. Between `m+1` and `m+2`, 25 more join and 24 others leave.
5. Enumerated against month `m`, the `(m+1, m+2)` row has joiners 30, leavers 30 and stayers 70. Each passes, so the row is published with these components.
6. For the truth, the adjacent parts of `(m+1, m+2)` give joiners 25, leavers 24 and stayers 75. No part runs from `m` to `m+2`.
7. Item 4's line `sum(cohort variables matching published month_change component l, months m and m+1) = A_cohort[l,m]` then requires 25 = 30, so the true assignment is INFEASIBLE.
8. Any assignment that meets that line has U's stayer and leaver parts out of month `m+1` summing to 70 + 30 = 100, against the true 99.

**Exact replacement text.** In item 11, replace this sentence, which wraps over several source lines:

> A unit and tier carried forward add no equality for the later month; their variables still satisfy items 6 and 7, and the next comparison runs from the month the release shows.

with:

> A unit and tier carried forward add no equality for the later month; their variables still satisfy items 6 and 7, and the next comparison runs from the month the release shows: that comparison is held by its own parts, as above, over the universe's tuples, with the month the release shows in place of `m` and the later month of the comparison in place of `m+1`, and the cohorts of each published leaf for that comparison, the `month_change` components and stayers included, are the sums of those parts and not of the parts of the adjacent pair.

**Notes on the replacement.**

- The anchor phrase "the next comparison runs from the month the release shows." occurs once in the file.
- PRV-121 needs no change: these parts are held "as above", so they are "item 11's origin-destination parts".
- With the replacement, the failing input is FEASIBLE:
  - The parts from `m` to `m+2` are 70 staying, 30 out and 30 in. They meet the tuple identities at `m` (100) and at `m+2` (100), and they sum to the published components.
  - The adjacent parts of `(m, m+1)` (94 stay, 6 out, 5 in) and of `(m+1, m+2)` (75 stay, 24 out, 25 in) still meet their tuple identities, with the true 99 at `m+1`.
  - The carried-forward month adds no leaf equality.

## Observations outside the verdict

All of these are pre-existing or concern test strength. No change is asked for in this round.

1. **Items 1 and 2.** Their linear forms cap by "a published wage-bill leaf `l`" with `A_wage[l,m,q]`. They do not say "that the release shows for month `t`", as item 11 now does. For a carried-forward month, the opening of PRV-113 ("item 11 governs a carried-forward month") is the reading that gives no cap. The same words in items 1 and 2 would make that explicit.
2. **Two workplace jobs in one tuple.** Item 1's binary `x_p` cannot hold two `workplace` jobs of the target in one aggregate-class tuple, which DAT-04 allows ("Workplace tables count one job per (person, employer group, month)").
3. **Missing indicator for item 6 tests.** "each non-empty changed cohort satisfies the linear tests of item 6" needs an indicator when a latent cohort can be empty, and the text does not write one. This sentence was already present at 710ac47.
4. **The empty-cohort fixture does not test the indicator.** The fixture sits on B01, where the per-part band bounds alone force the empty part to zero. A model that keeps the bounds but omits the empty-part indicator, which PRV-121 lists as a defect, is also INFEASIBLE on it. A copy on a B12/B12 tuple would detect that omission.
5. **Workplace group changers.** The text does not settle whether a group changer in `workplace` is a stayer (PRV-55) or a leaver plus a joiner (contributor `[person_token,employer_group_token]`, PRV-42). Item 11's "match it" admits either reading, so feasibility does not depend on the answer.
6. **Older wording elsewhere.** `TASKS.md` S6-T20 still reads "any ratio computed before release, is refused (PRV-127)". Decision 0023 and the OI-140 update keep the older wording as dated records.

Each file records status, signed patch equality, full source/joined objects, exact differing block offsets, lengths and hashes. ## Precheck failure and the lead's forced test difference (S2-P36 × S2-P37)

- The lead's precheck of `spec.final.json` (spec 2, WORK `c55475cd`) failed command 7: `custodian/tests/test_build_resume.py::test_reuse_log_survives_later_terms_exception`, no failure returned. Source: the lead's brief for spec 3 and the commit message of `1d90cdaa`. The precheck's own output is not in this spec's evidence folder.
- Cause: an interaction of the join. S2-P36 (`812f499c`, `eaa2c5ff`) makes a certificate `PinError` on a terms page an advisory: the bounded reader maps it to an attempt failure and the build goes on. S2-P37 (`089f624d`, `a9468028`) was built on `c171b9e5` without S2-P36, and two of its tests raised that `PinError` from the transport to stand for an exception after a row's data. On the joined head the first test got no failure. The second, `test_data_completion_survives_exception_before_terms`, passed only because the second row's own fault ended the build.
- Lead fix: `1d90cdaaedf31b11b1ac8dfb950c1bce1169f372` (parent `c55475cd`; Anthropic, the joiner; no cherry-pick original). It changes only `custodian/tests/test_build_resume.py` (M, 21 insertions, 16 deletions), and no source file. Both tests now raise the `PinError` from the terms step itself (`build._read_terms_apart`, through monkeypatch), which the sibling secret-guard test already does. The second test also asserts that the second row's URL was not fetched.

# S2-P41 — ledger input log

Pull request https://github.com/albarami/economic-investment-intelligence/pull/113. BASE `7ef9dc96c7ccccfc8f2709bb139db44da452638f` (the squash merge of train S2-12, pull request 112). WORK `9df561af6d1f5ed6b445d8b10e641dc927d3250c`, one work commit.

Why alone: main's hosted tests job failed twice on the same tree, the hosted run of main at 7ef9dc96, attempts 1 and 2. Custodian part 2 reported "counts unavailable in 600.1 s" while every other suite passed. A rerun cannot fix a limit fault, so S2-P41 leaves the S2 gate train and merges first as its own pull request (lead ruling L-1410).

## Commit inventory

- `9df561af6d1f5ed6b445d8b10e641dc927d3250c`: ci(tests): custodian tests run in three parts with a 1200 s limit each and a 720 s hosted watch (S2-P41, decision 0086).
  - Builder: OpenAI Codex GPT-6 Sol on login B. Round 1 was S2-P41.b1 (2056 s); round 2 was S2-P41.r2 (1696 s), applying the owner's limit decision relayed at 23:11 (lead ruling L-1404).
  - Committed by the lead after the lead's own verification.

## Review trail

- **S2-P41.rv1: APPROVED** on `9df561af6d1f5ed6b445d8b10e641dc927d3250c`, by Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5 on login B (916 s). The maker differs from the builder.
- The reviewer's own plants ran in a scratch copy and each was restored:
  - a module dropped from every part: exit 1, "custodian parts do not cover the whole collection";
  - a module kept in every part: exit 1, "custodian parts overlap";
  - a new test module added: exit 0, and its two tests land in exactly one part;
  - the kill on timeout disabled: exit 1 after 60.24 s, then exit 0 in 10.02 s once restored.
- Local part times were 235.10 s, 289.56 s and 264.81 s, for 3,690, 3,533 and 3,552 passed. That is 10,775 in total, equal to the whole collection.
- Two findings, neither rejecting:
  - F1, a nit: the printed share uses the suite's own timeout field, while the kill uses the per-runner limit function. Recorded as OI-371.
  - F2, documents: decision 0086 amends decision 0060 items 1 to 4, not only items 2 and 4. Recorded as OI-372, with the reviewer's proposed items 2, 3 and 5.
- The reviewer's proposed item 4 (the hosted job's 90-minute cap against the summed suite limits) is recorded as OI-373.

## S2-T19 — The tender host's one cipher suite, from live run 5 (lead, 2026-11-19)

Live run 5 of `./eii build-public` on `0fa689540e7a82c1ae9fe6b8079a8940d78337fc` (20:22 to 20:44) exited 1 with 241 PASS lines and one failing source, `tenders_pub`, refused with `http_status` after the pinned chain was in place. The lead called the tender transport for each of the six first list pages in both languages from its own shell: every call raised the transport fault `unreachable`, and a plain handshake with the tender context closed with `SSLZeroReturnError`. The same handshake from an interpreter whose default suite list holds `AES128-GCM-SHA256` succeeded (TLS 1.2, that suite); the project interpreter (Python 3.14.6, OpenSSL 3.5.7) offers only forward-secret TLS 1.2 suites, and the host accepts none of them.

Change: `chain_context` appends the one suite `TENDER_SUITE` after the default TLS 1.2 suites, keeps their order, the security level and the TLS 1.2 floor, and refuses with `certificate_chain_incomplete` when the list grew by anything else; document 04 section 2 states it. `custodian/tests/test_tender_chain.py` adds `test_the_tender_context_adds_only_the_hosts_one_suite` and the planted `test_a_wider_suite_list_is_refused`; the stand-in context of `custodian/tests/test_s2_t29_fix10.py::test_f2_tender_requires_root_chain` gains the suite-list members a real context has (its assertions unchanged).

## S2-T19 — Tender size words by language and non-empty page slots (2026-11-20)

Builder: OpenAI, GPT-6 (Codex), senior data engineer for public web sources, bilingual card parsing and strict provenance. Strict self-review persona: release-evidence reviewer rejecting weakened assertions, skips, raised bounds, invented page shapes and closure without red-then-green evidence. Independent review by another maker remains with the lead; self-review is not that approval.

Loaded skills: project-orientation, task-standards, github-flow, sanad-provenance, strict-reviewer and muhasabah-gate. Equivalent brief rules used where no skill was available: test-driven-development (new regression tests first), systematic-debugging (inspect supplied public shapes and trace parser/merge), verification-before-completion (actual commands and exits). The existing checkout is retained; no branch change, push or network call is authorized.

Evidence basis: base commit `537c0a7aebc10569a1beeb58581361635efcf05a`; the assigned brief; the six supplied public list-page copies in the lead's input folder of page copies (not in the repository), read only to model their structure; `docs/03_DATA_CONTRACTS.md`, `pub_tender`; and `docs/04_PUBLIC_DATA_PACK.md`, S2-T19 source reading and collection boundary. The supplied copies show three sibling size labels, some empty, and language-specific words: `Micro|Small|Medium` versus `متناهية الصغر|صغيرة|متوسطة`, `||Medium` versus `||متوسطة`, and `|Small|` versus `|صغيرة|`. No live request was made here, and no page identifiers, titles or other public-page text were copied into fixtures or this record. The lead's failed full build is evidence reported by the brief, not a run performed here.

Cause: `_row_for` treated `company_size` as a shared value across languages, so translated size words caused `company_size awarded`; `_pair` joined empty label slots as though they were words. Fix: compare size words with the existing per-language conflict check, evaluate both languages, then select English words or Arabic words if English has none. Drop empty normalized labels before joining; all-empty cards therefore have no size. Existing same-language conflicts still refuse with the same closed column/list reason, including an Arabic conflict when English supplies the selected words.

ASSUMPTION for review: the contract's "page-order size words joined by a vertical bar" means non-empty words only; an unselected empty label is not a word, and all-empty labels yield `None`. This is the lead's reading in the brief, proposed for contest in `builder workspace/RETURN.md` under PROPOSED OPEN ITEMS. No approved contract or decision was silently amended.

Environment: Linux x86_64; `uv` 0.11.31; test interpreter Python 3.14.6. Commands ran from the repository root with `UV_OFFLINE=1`, `UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=never`, workspace-local `UV_CACHE_DIR` and `TMPDIR`, and `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`. ## S2-T10 part F — OI-129: no sandboxed process outlives a driver killed during start-up (2026-11-20)

Builder: Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5 (overnight worker); persona a senior Linux sandboxing and security engineer; strict self-review as a security reviewer. Skills: project-orientation, task-standards, systematic-debugging, test-driven-development, security-review (plain meaning), verification-before-completion, muhasabah-gate. Base `33df1963`; environment: four processors of the build machine, bubblewrap 0.11.1, kernel 6.6 (WSL2), Python 3.14 from the project environment.

Cause (batch F12, reproduced again here): `scripts/sandbox_launch.py` started bubblewrap as the driver's direct child. Bubblewrap's `--die-with-parent` arms a parent-death signal in each of its layers, but the inner layer (the init of the new pid namespace) arms its own only during its start-up. A driver killed before that kills the outer layer, and the inner layer is re-parented to the system's init and runs the sandboxed command on. Every survivor was that inner `bwrap` with its sandboxed `python`.

Fix: the launcher starts `scripts/sandbox_supervisor.py`, which starts bubblewrap as its child. Before it starts anything the supervisor makes itself a child subreaper (checked by reading the flag back), arms a parent-death signal and checks the driver is still its parent, and checks a control pipe whose only writer is the driver; it refuses the run (status 1, `sandbox supervisor: ` line, nothing started) if any step fails. When the pipe reaches end of file (the driver exited, crashed or was killed, or closed it at its time limit) or an ending signal arrives, the supervisor kills every child it has, present or re-parented to it, and reaps until it has none: a subreaper with no child has no descendant, and killing the inner layer kills its whole pid namespace. Signals are routed to a wake-up pipe, never raised, so the ending cannot be interrupted half-way. The timeout path closes the pipe instead of killing a process group; its message is now "every process of the sandbox was killed". No bubblewrap option, mount, bound or time limit changed.

Red before (unchanged launcher, alone):
- new `test_driver_killed_while_a_layer_is_unarmed` (a stand-in bubblewrap whose inner layer never arms the signal; the deterministic reproduction, swapped in only in the test driver's own process): 30 runs, 30 failed.
- new `test_driver_killed_at_the_first_sandbox_process` (real bubblewrap, driver killed at the first process of the launch, no pause): 30 runs, 30 failed.
- unchanged `test_die_with_parent` with four CPU-bound busy loops on the same four processors: 30 runs, 5 failed ("a sandboxed process outlived its driver"); 4 surviving inner `bwrap` processes found re-parented to init afterwards and killed by pid.

Green after (fixed launcher, four CPU-bound busy loops on the same processors, killed by pid afterwards):
- unchanged `test_die_with_parent`: 30 runs, 0 failed.
- `test_driver_killed_while_a_layer_is_unarmed`: 30 runs, 0 failed.
- `test_driver_killed_at_the_first_sandbox_process`: 30 runs, 0 failed.
- no marker process left after any series.

Planted violations: the supervisor without the subreaper flag fails `test_driver_killed_while_a_layer_is_unarmed` and four tests of `scripts/tests/test_sandbox_supervisor.py`; the supervisor without the sweep of its children fails the same stand-in test and three supervisor tests; each plant was reverted and the file compared equal to the kept copy.

Checks on the final tree (exit codes): `uv run --locked python -m pytest scripts/tests/test_sandbox_*.py -p no:cacheprovider -q` 0 (87 passed, 16 subtests); `uv run --locked python scripts/sandbox_check.py check` 0, `check-extensions` 0, `check-enforcement` 0; `uv run --locked python -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py' -v` 0 (937 tests, OK); `uv run --locked ruff check .` 0; `uv run --locked ruff format --check .` 0; `uv run --locked mypy` 0 (447 files); `python3 scripts/check_docs.py` 0; `python3 scripts/check_tree.py` 0; `cmp AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md` 0. `./eii test` not run (brief). The two new marker tests join `ci_junit.REQUIRED` (21 cases). Independent review by another maker is still needed (rule 35).

## S2-T10 part F, fix round — OI-129: the launcher's cleanup after a timeout is bounded and setup errors are refused (2026-11-20)

Builder: Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5 (overnight worker, the maker of `d6383e44c5af9946c2cd0baac16ae998c1f72181`); persona a senior Linux systems engineer for process sandboxes; strict self-review as a security reviewer. Reviews answered: the first review of part F (another maker, REJECTED: F1, record notes N1 and N2) and the second (another maker, APPROVED: findings 1 and 2). Skills: test-driven-development and verification-before-completion applied as written; project-orientation, task-standards, systematic-debugging, security-review and muhasabah-gate in their plain meaning (not loaded).

Finding F1 (both reviews). Cause: at the time limit `scripts/sandbox_launch.py` closed the control pipe and then waited for the supervisor with `process.communicate()` and no bound, so a supervisor whose cleanup stalls (stopped, or blocked in `waitpid` on a process that does not end) held the launcher for good. Fix: the wait after the close is bounded by `CLEANUP_SECONDS` (4 s). When it expires, `end_stalled` stops the supervisor's process group, then walks `/proc` by parent from the supervisor, pins each descendant with a process descriptor, checks that it still has the parent the walk saw and stops it, until a walk finds no new one; it then kills every pinned process and the group, and reaps the supervisor, all within `KILL_SECONDS` (2 s). The walk is needed because bubblewrap's inner layer runs in a session of its own, which a kill of the group alone misses. The output is read for at most `DRAIN_SECONDS` (1 s); after that the streams are closed. The time-out then says "the supervisor's cleanup did not finish and its processes were killed by the launcher". If any signal was refused, the walk did not settle, the supervisor was not reaped or a pinned process did not end within the bound, it says instead that they "were sent a kill by the launcher, but their end is not confirmed". It never uses the normal text in either case. With a 1 s limit the sum stays within the existing 10 s of the time-out tests; no limit was raised. Test-only stand-in: `STALLED_SUPERVISOR` in `scripts/tests/sandbox_support.py` (ignores the closed pipe and the ending signals; one child in its group; one child in a new session with a child of its own), swapped in as `launch.SUPERVISOR` only inside `STALLED_DRIVER`, the test's own driver process.

Finding 2 of the second review. Cause: an exception in the supervisor's set-up before its `try` block (for example `os.pipe2` failing) ended it with a traceback instead of a refusal line. Fix: the set-up is wrapped; such an error refuses with "sandbox supervisor: the run was refused after an error in its set-up (TYPE)", where TYPE is the exception's class name, and nothing is started.

Record notes N1 and N2 of the first review: applied as written (the comment of `test_driver_killed_at_the_first_sandbox_process`; the `timeout` argument line of `run_in_sandbox`). The rename that the second review's record note suggested was not done.

Forced change to an existing test, with its reason: `test_sandbox_argv.ArgvRules.test_setup_failure_exit_and_timeout` case "f" pinned the second wait as `timeout=None`, which is the unbounded wait. It now expects `launch.CLEANUP_SECONDS`, so it asserts the bound. That is stricter than before, not weaker. Every other existing test, bound and refusal is unchanged. `test_die_with_parent` and `DIE_DRIVER` are byte-identical to `d6383e44` (same sha256 of the method and of the driver text).

New tests: `test_sandbox_mounts.MountRules.test_timeout_with_a_stalled_supervisor_is_bounded` (marked sandbox module; it joins `ci_junit.REQUIRED`, now 22 cases); `test_sandbox_supervisor.SupervisorRules.test_a_setup_error_is_refused_and_nothing_starts` and `test_the_launcher_ends_a_stalled_run_itself` (three cases: confirmed, a late supervisor, a refused stop signal). These two are in the unmarked module, so they are not in the required list.

Red, with the `d6383e44` launcher and supervisor and the new tests: `uv run --locked python -m pytest` on the three new tests exited 1. The stalled-supervisor test failed with "the launcher did not return after its supervisor stalled" when its 30 s bound on the driver ran out. The set-up test got a traceback and no refusal line. The `end_stalled` test failed with no such attribute. Nothing was left running.

Green after: the same tests pass. Planted violation: with the `/proc` walk turned off, so that only the group is killed, the stalled-supervisor test fails and lists the two processes of the other session as survivors. The plant was reverted and the file compared equal to the kept copy.

## S2-T10 part F, third round — OI-129: the stalled-run cleanup validates ancestry, carries its deadline and never confirms an unread process (2026-11-20)

Builder: Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5 (overnight worker, the maker of `c55f78675510ad19d1b69fb2347d2910e27886b1`); persona a senior Linux sandbox engineer (bubblewrap, pid namespaces, child subreapers, process descriptors, bounded cleanup); strict self-review as a security reviewer. Review answered: the third review of part F (another maker, REJECTED: F1 to F3 and record note N1), all accepted by the lead (ruling L-1203). Skills: test-driven-development and verification-before-completion applied as written; project-orientation, task-standards, systematic-debugging, security-review and muhasabah-gate in their plain meaning (not loaded).

F1. Cause: `end_stalled` took a whole numeric tree from one walk and then checked each process only against its parent's number, so the child of a rejected (reused) parent number was still stopped and killed. Fix: each round (`_walk_round`) reads `/proc` once and goes down from the unreaped supervisor through established processes only. A candidate is pinned by a process descriptor, read again, and kept only when it has not ended after the read, its start time (field 22 of `/proc/<pid>/stat`) equals the walk's, its live parent is the established parent's id, and that parent (pinned, or the unreaped supervisor) has not ended after the read. A candidate that is gone, stale or not established is neither signalled nor gone below; pins are keyed by id and start time. Test: `test_sandbox_supervisor.SupervisorRules.test_a_stale_tree_never_signals_an_unrelated_process` (root -> A -> B -> C, where B and C are an unrelated parent and child that the test started, C's parent really being B's number, and the walk's first read of B naming A as its parent; process descriptors signalled are traced through `/proc/self/fdinfo`).

F2. Cause: the deadline was checked only before each whole walk; enumeration, tree building, pinning and stopping had no check. Fix: one absolute deadline of `KILL_SECONDS` from the call; the walk stops at `WALK_SECONDS` (half of it), checked before each `/proc` entry is read and each candidate is pinned; a walk cut short is not settled, so the end is unconfirmed. The kills (one call per pinned process and one to the group) are always sent and timed: sent after the deadline, the end is unconfirmed; the waits use what is left. No limit was raised (`CLEANUP_SECONDS` 4, `KILL_SECONDS` 2, `DRAIN_SECONDS` 1, unchanged). Test: `test_the_walk_stops_at_its_deadline` (the clock passes the whole bound at the third stat read; no process is read after it, the group's kill is still sent, the result is False, under 2 s of real time).

F3. Cause: `_parent_of` took every `OSError` as a gone process. Fix: `_stat_of` returns None only for ENOENT and ESRCH; any other error or a malformed line raises `_Unread`, which makes the round incomplete, so the walk cannot settle and the launcher cannot say "killed". A supervisor already reaped, or one found ended during the walk, is not walked from and leaves the end unconfirmed. Test: `test_an_unreadable_process_is_never_confirmed` (EACCES on the stat of the stand-in's child in a session of its own; the result is False and that child is indeed still running, then ended by the test).

Red, with the `c55f7867` launcher and the three new tests: exit 1, 3 failed: F1 the unrelated child was signalled; F2 106 stat reads after the deadline; F3 `end_stalled` returned True. Green after: `test_sandbox_supervisor.py` exit 0 (13 passed, 3 subtests). Planted violations in the new launcher, each reverted and compared equal to the kept copy: going below a stale candidate fails the F1 test (the unrelated child signalled); no deadline check in the enumeration fails the F2 test; an unreadable stat taken as gone fails the F3 test (True returned). The three new tests are in the unmarked module, so `ci_junit.REQUIRED` is unchanged (22 cases, none lost). `test_die_with_parent`, `DIE_DRIVER`, `test_sandbox_mounts.py` and `sandbox_support.py` are unchanged.

Repeat series on the final code, 30 runs each, run by unittest in one process with four CPU-bound busy loops on the four processors of the affinity mask (all four alive at the end, killed by pid afterwards; no busy loop or marker process left): `test_die_with_parent`, `test_driver_killed_while_a_layer_is_unarmed`, `test_driver_killed_at_the_first_sandbox_process`, `test_timeout_with_a_stalled_supervisor_is_bounded`, `test_timeout_kills_the_process_group`, `test_a_setup_error_is_refused_and_nothing_starts`, `test_the_launcher_ends_a_stalled_run_itself` and the three new tests: 0 failed each.

Checks on the final tree (exit codes): `uv run --locked python -m pytest scripts/tests/test_sandbox_supervisor.py scripts/tests/test_sandbox_mounts.py scripts/tests/test_sandbox_argv.py scripts/tests/test_sandbox_prove.py -q -p no:cacheprovider` 0 (44 passed, 3 subtests); `uv run --locked python scripts/sandbox_check.py check-enforcement` 0 ("sandbox enforcement: OK"); `uv run --locked python -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py'` 0 (943 tests, OK); `uv run --locked ruff check .` 0; `uv run --locked ruff format --check .` 0 (after the formatter was applied to `scripts/sandbox_launch.py`; its first run exited 1 on that file); `uv run --locked mypy` 0 (447 files); `python3 scripts/check_docs.py` 0 (1126 text files, 120 Markdown files); `python3 scripts/check_tree.py` 0 (8 rules); `cmp AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md` 0. `./eii test` not run (brief). ## S2-T10 part F, fourth round — OI-129: one deadline bounds the whole stalled-run cleanup (2026-11-20)

Builder: Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5 (overnight worker, the maker of `34294ca91d2838436a49f94e1532f3d95f5dde9b`); persona a senior Linux sandbox engineer; strict self-review as a security reviewer. Skills: project-orientation, task-standards, test-driven-development, systematic-debugging, verification-before-completion, muhasabah-gate; security-review in its plain meaning. Review answered: the fourth part F review (another maker, REJECTED: "F2 — NOT FIXED"; F1 and F3 closed). Only F2 was changed (ruling L-1206).

F2. Cause: at `34294ca9` the deadline bounded only the enumeration of `/proc` and each candidate. After an expired enumeration, `_walk_round` still built the parent index from the whole partial table. It sorted each sibling list before any check, and it took frontier entries with `pop(0)` and no check, so leaf entries were drained after the deadline. The kills and closes of the finalization had no bound fixed before processes were taken. Fix in `scripts/sandbox_launch.py`: `_process_table` places each process under its parent as it is read, inside the deadline-checked loop (`_Table`); the frontier is a `deque` and the deadline is checked before every entry is taken and before every candidate; nothing is sorted. A new constant `TARGET_SLOTS` (512) bounds the kill-and-close work before another process is stopped: each taken process holds one kill slot, the group's kill has its own, and a walk that runs out of slots stops (`_Round.full`), still kills every taken process and the group, closes their descriptors and returns unconfirmed. The waits use only what is left before the deadline. No bound was raised: `CLEANUP_SECONDS` 4, `KILL_SECONDS` 2, `DRAIN_SECONDS` 1, `WALK_SECONDS` `KILL_SECONDS / 2`.

Tests (`scripts/tests/test_sandbox_supervisor.py`, unmarked module): `test_the_index_is_not_built_after_the_deadline` (plant (a): the clock passes the whole bound as the third process read is placed under its parent; no process may be placed after it); `test_the_frontier_stops_at_the_deadline` (plant (b): the clock passes the bound as the last process of the run is stopped, which leaves it, a leaf, on the frontier; no frontier entry may be taken after it, and every stopped process and the group are still killed); `test_the_kill_work_is_bounded_before_a_process_is_taken` (plant (c): two target slots; the walk takes the two children of the stand-in and not the third process; the clock passes the bound at the first kill; both taken processes and the group are still killed, two descriptors are closed, every wait gets a time-out of 0, the result is False and the untaken process is indeed still running, then ended by the test); `test_the_cleanup_time_is_bounded` (a virtual clock that never moves by itself and moves only by a fixed cost per stat read, process descriptor and signal and by the whole time-out of each blocking wait; for a run that settles and one that never settles, an unreadable process, the cleanup ends within `KILL_SECONDS` of that clock and kills every stopped process and the group; no sleep-based timing).

Red, with the `34294ca9` launcher and the four new tests: exit 1, 3 failed, 1 passed (2 subtests). Plant (a) failed with 113 processes indexed after the deadline; plant (b) failed with one leaf frontier entry processed after the deadline; plant (c) failed with three processes taken against two slots. The bound test passed on `34294ca9` as well; it is not one of the plants. Green after: `test_sandbox_supervisor.py` exit 0 (17 passed, 5 subtests). Planted violations in the new launcher, each reverted and compared equal to the kept copy, each exit 1: indexing moved after discovery fails (a); the frontier check removed fails (b); the slot check removed fails (c); the reaping wait given `KILL_SECONDS` instead of what is left fails the bound test in both cases (2.2578125 and 3.001953125 against 2.0). `test_die_with_parent`, `DIE_DRIVER`, `test_sandbox_mounts.py`, `sandbox_support.py` and `scripts/ci_junit.py` are unchanged, so `ci_junit.REQUIRED` keeps its 22 cases.

Repeat series on the final code, 30 runs each, run by unittest in one process with four CPU-bound busy loops on the four processors of the affinity mask (all four alive at the end, killed by pid afterwards; no busy loop or marker process left): `test_die_with_parent`, `test_driver_killed_while_a_layer_is_unarmed`, `test_driver_killed_at_the_first_sandbox_process`, `test_timeout_with_a_stalled_supervisor_is_bounded`, `test_timeout_kills_the_process_group`, `test_a_setup_error_is_refused_and_nothing_starts`, `test_the_launcher_ends_a_stalled_run_itself`, `test_a_stale_tree_never_signals_an_unrelated_process`, `test_the_walk_stops_at_its_deadline`, `test_an_unreadable_process_is_never_confirmed` and the four new tests: 0 failed each.

Checks on the final tree (exit codes; Python 3.14.6, WSL2 kernel 6.6): `uv run --locked python -m pytest scripts/tests/test_sandbox_supervisor.py scripts/tests/test_sandbox_mounts.py scripts/tests/test_sandbox_argv.py scripts/tests/test_sandbox_prove.py -q -p no:cacheprovider` 0 (48 passed, 5 subtests); `uv run --locked python scripts/sandbox_check.py check-enforcement` 0 ("sandbox enforcement: OK"); `uv run --locked python -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py'` 0 (947 tests, OK); `uv run --locked ruff check .` 0; `uv run --locked ruff format --check .` 0 (after the formatter was applied to the test file; its first run exited 1 on it); `uv run --locked mypy` 0 (447 files); `python3 scripts/check_docs.py` 0 (1126 text files, 120 Markdown files); `python3 scripts/check_tree.py` 0 (8 rules); `cmp AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md` 0. `./eii test` not run (brief). ## S2-T10 part F, fifth round — OI-129: the closes after the waits end within the cleanup deadline (2026-11-20)

Builder: Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5 (the lead, deciding the last finding of round four by reproduction on the deterministic clock, as the round-four ruling set); persona a senior Linux sandbox engineer; strict self-review as a security reviewer. Skills: test-driven-development, systematic-debugging, verification-before-completion, muhasabah-gate.

F2, remaining path (fifth review, on `c5968f98`): `process.wait` and the polls of `_ended` were given every second left before the absolute deadline, and the descriptor of every taken process was closed after them in `finally`, so a wait that used its whole allowance left the closes past the deadline; the result's timeliness was taken before the waits and closes. Reproduction: the bound test charges each close one step of its virtual clock; on `c5968f98` it fails, elapsed 2.0029296875 and 2.0009765625 against `KILL_SECONDS` 2.0 (exit 1, 2 failed, 1 passed).

Fix (`scripts/sandbox_launch.py`): a new constant `CLOSE_SECONDS = KILL_SECONDS / 16` is kept back from the same deadline: the waits and polls end `CLOSE_SECONDS` before it, the closes follow, and the result is True only when every earlier condition held and the clock after the closes is still within the deadline. No bound raised: `CLEANUP_SECONDS` 4, `KILL_SECONDS` 2, `DRAIN_SECONDS` 1, `WALK_SECONDS` 1, `TARGET_SLOTS` 512 unchanged; the waits only end sooner, and a run ending in that last part is reported unconfirmed. Measured basis: 512 closes of process descriptors on this machine took 0.102 ms in all, far inside the 0.125 s kept; that the closes never block is an assumption of the host, as the fifth review's open item states.

Test: `test_the_cleanup_time_is_bounded` charges every close and checks that at least one taken process was closed. Red on `c5968f98`, green here (`test_sandbox_supervisor.py` exit 0, 17 passed, 5 subtests); plant `CLOSE_SECONDS = 0.0`: exit 1, 2 failed, the same two elapsed values; reverted and compared equal to the kept file.

Checks on the final tree: the four sandbox test files `-q -p no:cacheprovider` exit 0, 48 passed, 5 subtests; `sandbox_check.py check-enforcement` exit 0, "sandbox enforcement: OK"; `ruff check .` exit 0; `ruff format --check .` exit 0, 829 files; `mypy` exit 0, 447 files; `check_docs.py` exit 0; `check_tree.py` exit 0; `cmp AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md` exit 0; `unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py'` exit 0, Ran 947 tests, OK. `./eii test` is run by the lead on the train.

- Cause: the heavy overlay was attached while the basemap's source/style startup was still active. Basemap startup frames therefore also redrew the entire data scene. The old first-idle interval was 26592.9/31095.4 ms without/with owned load. A loaded scratch change attaching on the basemap load event gave 705.0 ms first idle and 40712.1 ms readiness for full street. The implemented load-event ordering gives 752.6/796.4 ms first idle and 40761.9/38585.3 ms readiness. The slow per-frame intervals in the retained render marks disappear from startup, rather than being hidden by a new readiness condition. Some rendering moves to the existing orbit interval; total host readiness is recorded above. Both actual samples still make all 256 reads, 512 per scene, and only each sample's first read is slow. All measured scenes retain 110000 hexagons, 50000 particles, 250004 or 100004 roads and positive hex/particle/road samples. This is a tested startup-order cause, not per-point read overhead.
- Implementation: `web/spikes/performance/layers.ts` registers the existing error guard before waiting on basemap load, then mounts the unchanged overlay and waits for idle before reading rendered counts. A load failure removes deferred load and idle callbacks; a synchronous overlay-mount exception rejects the same readiness promise. Existing success listener-removal expectation, sampling, layer-count code, browser specs/config, time limits and evidence remain unchanged. `web/spikes/performance/README.md` explains this lifecycle.
